need: The changed check and the test-first check compare a branch with the commit it started from, so that merges into the base branch after the branch started are not counted as the branch's own changes.

searched.where: ~/code2/agentic-engineering-system-canonical: `grep -rn merge-base src/lockstep scripts` at the head of branch lockstep-changed-requirements; src/lockstep/checks/test_first.py and changed.py read in full
searched.query: does any Lockstep check already resolve a base revision to the branch's starting commit
searched.found: No use in src/lockstep. scripts/lane_sweep.py, prune_merged_worktrees.py and refresh_canonical_checkouts.py call `git merge-base` for other questions (is a branch merged, where did a lane fork). scripts/md_file_cap.py records that the older Lockstep's `make check` passed `--base $(git merge-base ...)` from the Makefile. test_first.py and changed.py unpack the revision exactly as given.

searched.where: git's own manual on this machine: `git help diff` (the `--merge-base` option and the `<commit>...<commit>` form) and `git help merge-base`
searched.query: how git itself compares a branch with the point where it left another branch
searched.found: `git diff --merge-base A` is documented as equivalent to `git diff $(git merge-base A HEAD)`; `git merge-base A HEAD` prints that commit and exits non-zero when there is no common ancestor.

candidates.name: git merge-base
candidates.covers: Returns the commit a branch started from, given the base branch and HEAD; already installed everywhere Lockstep runs.
candidates.misses: Nothing for this need. It exits non-zero with no shared history; the checks then fall back to the revision as given.
candidates.reason: It is the standard answer and one subprocess call.

candidates.name: Passing the merge base from each repository's Makefile (`--base $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD)`)
candidates.covers: The same comparison, with no change to Lockstep.
candidates.misses: Every repository's Makefile has to get it right; one that passes `origin/main` plainly fails on every branch behind main, with findings that name other people's requirements.
candidates.reason: The mistake is easy and its findings are misleading; resolving it once inside the check removes it for every repository.
